title: Amsterdam Imaging Hub
text:
The Amsterdam Imaging Hub was founded by researchers from AMOLF and Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI), later joined by colleagues from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (VU). We work in many different domains across physics, materials science, and computer vision and are all united by a powerful common thread: reliance on imaging. We recognized that powerful imaging methods were being developed across all disciplines but often in isolation rather than being shared across fields.
We created this community to fix that gap.
Our goal is straightforward: connect people working with imaging across Amsterdam and enable real exchange and promotion of practical knowledge, tools, and expertise.
So far, we have organized three Imaging Symposia that brought together more than a hundred researchers from astronomy, computational imaging, physics, archaeology, materials science, medicine, biology, and electron microscopy. In addition, we organize hands-on tutorials and Imaging Lunches, fostering learning of the latest developments in the field and building new collaborations.

title: Courses
text:
Spring 2026
This course is about inverse problems in imaging. The mathematical reconstruction and processing of images is of fundamental importance in state of the art applications in health and geosciences, e.g. in medical tomography, in high-resolution microscopy or in geophysical inversion. In many cases, underlying inverse problems can be formulated and solved using variational methods and partial differential equations. This course offers a theoretical as well as an applied insight into inverse problems and variational methods for mathematical imaging. It addresses reconstruction problems of different imaging modalities (e.g. CT or PET) in biomedicine and geophysics.

title: Annual Imaging Symposium
text:
The annual imaging symposium took place on February 20th at the VU.

Program
09.30 – 09.45 - Walk in coffee
09.45 – 10.00 - Introduction
10:00 – 10:30 - Daniela Huppenkothen (UvA) Imaging in Astronomy
10:30 – 11:00 - Peter Kraus (ARCNL) When Resolution Is (Not) Everything: Imaging Complex Materials and Devices
11:00 – 11:30 - Short break
11:30 – 12:00 - Martijn de Bruin (Amsterdam UMC) Imaging Tomorrow: How Technology Is Redefining Diagnosis and therapy
12:00 – 14:30 - Lunch Break & Posters
14:30 – 15:00 - Kristina Ganzinger (AMOLF) Live microscopy: cracking the challenge to image biology unfolding in cells, tissues and organoids
15:00 – 15:30 - Mason Scholte (UvA) Practical imaging in archaeology: Examples from the 4D Research Lab
15:30 – 16:00 - Brainstorm session “Building the Hub:” Events, Education, etc.
16:00 – 17:00 - Borrel & Posters
